introduction: The AMR Pro is the circuit-only version of the Valkyrie hypercar. Aston Martin removed the road car's hybrid system, lengthened the wheelbase and widened the tracks, leaving a Cosworth V12 revving to 11,000 rpm and an aero package aimed at Le Mans prototype lap times.

drawings.label: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro, side elevation

powertrain.label: Hybrid system
powertrain.value: Removed (road car's battery-electric system deleted to save weight)

chassis.label: Wheelbase change
chassis.value: 380 mm longer than the Valkyrie road car

chassis.label: Track change
chassis.value: 96 mm wider at the front, 115 mm wider at the rear than the road car

chassis.label: Body
chassis.value: Carbon-fibre bodywork with carbon-fibre suspension wishbones and Perspex glazing

entries.title: Concept shown at Geneva
entries.detail: Aston Martin first presented the track-only AMR Pro at the 2018 Geneva Motor Show as a companion to the Valkyrie road car developed with Red Bull Advanced Technologies.

entries.title: Production version revealed
entries.detail: In June 2021 the company detailed the reworked production car, now without hybrid assistance, and set a run of 40 cars plus two prototypes, with first deliveries planned for the end of that year.

entries.title: Le Mans lap target
entries.detail: Aston Martin said the car was designed to lap the 13.6 km Circuit de la Sarthe in roughly 3 minutes 20 seconds.
